correctness.limitations: The proof is analytic: the frozen finite checker was inspected, not executed. The order is for the specified canonical continuous conditional law at every positive sum and for equal-rate bivariate exponential margins. Strict coordinatewise coupling does not imply strict expectation for every monotone function. For θ<0 the ratio is decreasing only on the common interior; it is not claimed to give reverse LR order with the unequal supports.
correctness.rationale: A positive scale change reduces the rate to one. Differentiating the given copula and changing variables to (X,S) cancels the common factor e^(-s) on the slice; H=1+θ(1−2u)(1−2v)>0 on 0<x<s even for |θ|=1. Set A=1−2u. Direct differentiation gives H_x=2θ(u−v), H_s=2θvA, H_xs=2θv, hence H² times the mixed log derivative equals 2θv(1+θA²). Integrating in s yields the positive/zero/negative sign for the common-support likelihood ratio because normalizers do not depend on x. Nested support extends the increasing ratio to the new right tail for θ≥0; even the constant common-support ratio at θ=0 implies strict CDF order by the positive added tail, since the conditional larger-sum law restricted to the old support is already weakly stochastically larger there. For θ=−r, integration of the explicit mixture of H_0 and H_−1 gives N=(1−r)t+2r(c+zd) and Z=(1−r)s+4r[1−(1+s)z]. Expanding the derivative numerator in (1−r)², r(1−r), and r² gives exactly the three negative terms in RESULT.md. With d<0, (1+s)z decreases and c+(1+t)e^(−t)d is positive by the stated positive Taylor tail. The last brace sc+(1−z)d starts positive at s=t and its derivative is bounded below by 2[1−(1+t)e^(−t)]>0. With d≥0 it is immediate. At r=0 or 1 the remaining term is strictly negative. Thus the CDF strictly decreases at each t in the common interior; between supports the strict difference follows from positive density. The continuous strictly increasing CDFs make each interior quantile strictly increase with s. Exchangeable symmetry gives Q_s(1−a)=s−Q_s(a); using one U and the two probabilities U and 1−U realizes both conditionals with strictly increasing coordinates.

value.rationale: The dependent version of conditional-sum monotonicity is an established risk-allocation and stochastic-order problem. The entire negative dependence range gives a motivated, exact separation: each sum increase permits strict simultaneous coordinate growth, while the increasing conditional likelihood-ratio order fails for every distinct pair of sums. This establishes more than a finite case or a restatement of a sufficient positive-dependence criterion.
